back: A business owned by one person, who keeps all the profit and has unlimited liability.
A business owned by two or more partners who share capital, work, decisions and profit; usually unlimited liability.
A business owned and controlled by its members, with one vote each, for their mutual benefit; surplus shared among members.
Shareholders can lose only the money they invested; their personal possessions are safe.
The owners are personally responsible for all the debts of the business.
Both have limited liability and are separate legal entities; only a public company can sell shares to the public.
External matters: name, registered office, objects, share capital and limited liability.
Internal rules: directors' powers, meetings, voting, dividends and share transfers.

front: Certificate of incorporation and trading certificate
back: Incorporation creates the company in law; a trading certificate lets a public company start business.
